source.title: Masterful: A Training Platform for Computer Vision Models
source.authors: S. Wookey; Yaoshiang Ho; Thomas D. Rikert; Juan David Gil Lopez; Juan Manuel Munoz Beancur; Santiago Cortés; R. Tawil; Aaron Sabin; Jack Lynch; Travis Harper; Nikhil Gajendrakumar

record.file_problem: Full text is present. The results table has a batch-size layout ambiguity, noted in the row notes.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy for EfficientNetB0 on CIFAR-10 under two batch-size setups, bearing on V1's training-error outcome; it does not reproduce the cited recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training accuracy for two setups. Its table lists batch size 64 for both rows, while the surrounding text identifies the experimental batch size as 1024; the mapping is therefore recorded with that ambiguity. Other optimization discussion is explanatory or cites prior work, not additional results.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks its batch-size selection method using LAMB, reporting training accuracy and time after 81–82 epochs. It does not establish random initialization, use SGD or Adam, or assess convergence to near-zero training error under V1's conditions. Its other optimization statements are assumptions or descriptions of prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the experimental conclusion: the authors report comparable validation accuracy with approximately 75% less wall-clock time using the optimized batch-size setup. They do not conclude that these experiments establish near-zero training error.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LAMB and compares batch-size setups; the text does not state initialization. It does not reproduce the cited SGD or Adam training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The two batch-size setups and their starting learning rates differ; the table's batch-size mapping is ambiguous.

fits_no_version.finding: EfficientNetB0 trained with LAMB achieved training accuracies of 97.92% and 98.64%. The optimized batch-size setup reached 71.51% validation accuracy in 1914 seconds, versus 70.68% in 7416 seconds for the baseline; starting learning rates also differed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-noise-scale-guided batch-size selection, coupled with a higher starting learning rate, can reduce wall-clock training time while attaining similar validation accuracy.

record.problems: The training-accuracy results are reported in a flattened table with conflicting batch-size entries; no uncertainty is given, and the text does not state initialization.
record.rows_left_out: No other qualifying outcomes are reported. The cited results from prior work and optimization explanations are not this study's own results.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error with SGD or Adam from random initialization; CIFAR-100 and corrupted labels; effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of initialization on training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery, curvature changes, and divergence relative to a learning-rate stability threshold.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization or Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The general assertion in Section 8 that low-learning-rate full-batch training eventually reaches minimum loss is assumed, not demonstrated. The batch-size benchmark does not test V5 because no stability threshold, curvature trajectory, or recovery from instability is measured.

versions.untested_parts: Random initialization, SGD or Adam, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not tested.

rows.subject: EfficientNetB0
rows.operation_detail: Trained with LAMB at the common default batch size.
rows.note: The table reports 64 for this row; surrounding text describes batch size 64 as the baseline. The result is high training accuracy but does not establish zero error.
rows.check: The 97.92% training accuracy is correctly extracted, but this LAMB benchmark does not establish V1's specified training conditions or convergence. Nonzero error after 82 epochs alone does not demonstrate a limitation of V1.

rows.subject: EfficientNetB0
rows.operation_detail: Trained with LAMB using the batch size predicted by the gradient noise scale algorithm.
rows.note: The prose identifies 1024 as the predicted experimental batch size, but the flattened table lists 64 in both rows. The table-to-condition mapping is ambiguous; accuracy is high but does not establish zero error.
rows.check: The 98.64% training accuracy is correctly extracted, but this LAMB benchmark does not establish V1's specified training conditions or convergence. The prose specifies experimental batch size 1024, whereas the table prints 64; retain that source inconsistency.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: EfficientNetB0 on CIFAR-10 in the two reported batch-size setups
reader_labels.reason: Training accuracy was 97.92 % and 98.64 %, respectively; these are high but nonzero error rates, and the tested optimizer and setup do not cover the version's stated SGD/Adam and initialization conditions.
